# Deployment

This repository contains the public source, tests, and public-safe Wrangler templates for the cyspbot root page, Token Endpoint Proxy, GitHub webhook receiver, and GitHub webhook processor. It does not contain production domains, routes, Cloudflare resource identifiers, or secret values.

## Deployable Workers

`@cyspbot/cyspbot` deploys Worker `cyspbot` as the Custom Domain origin for the root page and Token Endpoint Proxy. Its [service contract](service-contract.md#routes) owns request matching and responses.

`@cyspbot/github-webhook-receiver` deploys Worker `cyspbot-github-webhook-receiver` for `POST /github/webhooks`.

`@cyspbot/github-webhook-processor` deploys Worker `cyspbot-github-webhook-processor` as the consumer for the status-reaction job queue.

The source-owned Worker configurations define their entrypoints, compatibility dates and flags, required binding names, safe local/dry-run service targets, and safe local values for the root proxy and processor's token-client variables. Production deployment configuration replaces those targets and supplies the deployment-owned endpoint values, audience, and issuer properties.

## Separate deployment pipeline

[`chikachow/cyspbot-deploy`](https://github.com/chikachow/cyspbot-deploy) pins this repository as a submodule and owns production Worker code, bindings, variables, validation, deployment workflows, and smoke probes. [`chikachow/infrastructure`](https://github.com/chikachow/infrastructure) manages the queues, retention, queue consumer, Custom Domain, and routes with Terraform. The webhook Route selects the receiver, and the retained Token Endpoint Route selects the cyspbot Worker. A cyspbot source update must pass its own checks and strict Wrangler dry runs in the deployment repository before deployment.

The source workflow `.github/workflows/run-cyspbot-deploy-update.yml` is responsible for dispatching the deployment repository's source-update workflow after successful `main` CI. It obtains a short-lived GitHub token through `cyspbot-app-token-action`.

The production deployment configuration retains the root Worker's broker HTTP
Service Binding, the receiver's queue producer binding, and the processor's
WorkloadIdentityIssuer RPC and broker Service Bindings. Terraform owns the processor's queue consumer attachment and its
retry and dead-letter settings. The source Wrangler consumer declaration is
for local tests and dry runs; production overlays omit consumers and routes.
The deployment configuration supplies the logical Workload Identity Token
audience and broker Token Endpoint URL as
separate variables. The issuer binding supplies the `WorkloadIdentityIssuer`
RPC together with its `subject` and `allowedAudiences` properties, while the
broker binding supplies the broker transport. The broker verifies the workload
identity assertion and performs authorization at its Token Endpoint.

## Delivery recovery

The deployment operator owns recovery of failed webhook deliveries and exhausted queue jobs. GitHub does not automatically redeliver failed webhooks; this source does not run a delivery-recovery scheduler. Queue durability starts only after the receiver successfully publishes the job.

After resolving an ingress failure, inspect the GitHub App's recent webhook deliveries and manually redeliver the failed delivery. See [GitHub's redelivery procedure](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/testing-and-troubleshooting-webhooks/redelivering-webhooks).

Every failed valid job retries and reaches `cyspbot-github-webhook-jobs-dlq` if
it exhausts the queue's retry budget. Inspect the DLQ and bounded processor
diagnostics, resolve the cause, then choose which jobs to replay through the
primary queue or deliberately discard. Replay requests credentials again and
does not bypass authorization. There is no job-age cutoff or automatic DLQ
replay. Invalid queue jobs are rejected before token acquisition and are not
retained for replay.

For manual replay, publish the unchanged job body to the primary queue and
confirm publication before acknowledging the DLQ copy. If publication or
acknowledgement has an ambiguous outcome, a duplicate is possible; repeating
the same reaction under the same GitHub App identity is safe. Do not purge a
DLQ job before its replay is durably published.

Monitor the DLQ backlog for recovery work. A `github_webhook_job_retrying` log
records a retry request, not confirmation of a DLQ transfer, including on the
last attempt. Unconsumed DLQ messages expire when their retention period ends.

Primary-queue retention also limits recovery: a job can expire before exhausting
its retries when delivery is delayed or consumers are unavailable. DLQ retention
does not extend that primary-queue window. Verify both retention settings against
the intended recovery window; this policy does not guarantee indefinite delivery.

The operator inspects the DLQ at least every 24 hours. Automated alerts are
currently unconfigured; recovery does not depend on email notification. Queue
retention is managed in Terraform, not by the Worker deployment pipeline.

Broker policy must authorize the processor's workload identity for the intended repositories and the exact requested scope, `issues:write pull_requests:write`. Keep both permissions until issue and pull-request conversation-comment behavior has been verified against the deployed GitHub App and broker policy.

## Local validation only

This repository's deployment command is a dry run:

```bash
fnm exec --using=24 pnpm run deploy:dry-run
```

Do not add production credentials, domains, or routes to this repository.

## Token Endpoint Proxy prerequisites

The cyspbot Worker's Token Endpoint Proxy requires a canonical HTTPS Token Endpoint
variable and a `GITHUB_APP_TOKEN_BROKER` HTTP Service Binding to the broker's
default handler. The binding selects the Worker; the URL selects its App path.
Deploy source and binding configuration together. An arbitrary public HTTPS
broker target is not supported by this proxy transport, and there is no public
fetch fallback. The broker's public canonical endpoint remains available to
its direct clients. Do not add an issuer binding or a named RPC entrypoint to
the root Worker for forwarding.

Verify the complete public ingress path preserves the original client's
`CF-Connecting-IP` and replaces spoofed client identity headers. The broker owns
admission with a shared `unknown` bucket for missing identity. Local fixtures and
synthetic remote-binding probes cannot establish edge identity authenticity.
See `SECURITY.md` for the trust boundary and public-ingress control limitations.

Terraform manages the production Custom Domains and Routes separately from
Worker publication. The retained vanity Token Endpoint Route selects the cyspbot
Worker. The [deployment repository](https://github.com/chikachow/cyspbot-deploy#token-endpoint-verification)
owns production verification of binding reachability, canonical and vanity OAuth
responses, edge admission identity, and the webhook-to-reaction flow.

# cyspbot deployment pipeline

This private repository deploys the `chikachow/cyspbot` root page, Token Endpoint Proxy, GitHub
webhook receiver, and GitHub webhook processor to production. The `cyspbot`
Worker owns the root page and `/token` convenience forwarding through its broker HTTP Service Binding. The separate
`chikachow/github-app-token-broker-deploy` pipeline publishes the canonical broker
App endpoint. Terraform manages the Custom Domains and webhook route.

The source implementation is pinned as the `src/cyspbot` git submodule. This
repository owns the production Wrangler configuration overlays, Cloudflare
resource identifiers and GitHub Actions deployment workflows.
[Infrastructure](https://github.com/chikachow/infrastructure) manages the queues,
queue consumer, Custom Domain and routes.

## Source

`src/cyspbot` pins the source commit that is eligible for production
deployment. Updating that submodule updates the source revision this repository
builds, checks, dry-runs, and deploys. The normal updater selects source `main`. This repository does not impose
an additional source-ancestry gate.

Install the [pinned pnpm version](#dependency-tooling) first.

```bash
git submodule update --init --recursive
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
node --run source:install
node --run check
node --run source:check
node --run deploy:dry-run
```

See [dependency tooling](#dependency-tooling) for the dependency update policy
and validation gates.

`node --run knip` checks deployment-owned scripts, dependencies and exports as
part of `check` and the single CI job. `knip.jsonc` lists the deployment CLI and
actual Node test pattern so unused helper files and exports are reported.
Wrangler runs from the separately checked source submodule and is therefore
excluded from the deployment binary dependency report.

## Workers

The three deployed Workers are listed in
`scripts/deploy-configuration.mjs`. Production bindings, variables, and Cloudflare resource identifiers live in
`config/workers/*.wrangler.jsonc`.

Worker `cyspbot` serves the `cyspbot.chikachow.org` Custom Domain as its
origin for the root page and `/token`. The more specific `/github/webhooks*`
Worker Route executes first and selects the webhook receiver.

Each Worker config filename must match the Worker name:
`config/workers/<worker-name>.wrangler.jsonc`.

The processor uses broker and `WorkloadIdentityIssuer` Service Bindings configured
in its production overlay. The root Worker uses a broker HTTP Service Binding without an issuer binding.
The broker still verifies subject tokens and applies its issuance policy; transport
reachability grants no token-issuance permission. The binding selects the broker
Worker, while the canonical endpoint URL selects its App path. Trusted binding
callers can supply admission identity headers; public callers must receive
edge-established identity at cyspbot ingress. The internal hop does not traverse
the broker hostname's public ingress controls. See the source [Token Exchange Client](https://github.com/chikachow/cyspbot/blob/main/docs/implementation.md#token-exchange-client)
for the protocol contract.

The deployment script runs a strict Wrangler dry-run for every configured Worker
before a production deploy. `node --run deploy:dry-run` stops after the dry-runs.
`node --run deploy` runs the dry-runs first, then deploys every Worker with
Wrangler strict checks enabled.

## Cloudflare Configuration

The production Wrangler overlays bind existing Cloudflare resources. Keep those
values in `config/workers/*.wrangler.jsonc`, not duplicated in documentation.
Worker secret values are supplied by Cloudflare Secrets Store; do not add secret
values to the Wrangler overlays.

## Local Deployment

Authenticate Wrangler locally:

```bash
node scripts/source-pnpm.mjs exec wrangler login
```

For non-interactive deployments, provide the Cloudflare credentials consumed by
Wrangler. The deploy scripts run Node with `--env-file-if-exists=.env`, and
explicit environment variables take precedence over `.env` values.

```bash
node --run source:install
node --run deploy:dry-run
node --run deploy
```

## GitHub Actions

CI is orchestrated by `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Its single `ci` job installs
frozen source dependencies, runs the full `source:check`, installs frozen private
dependencies, runs `check` including the private Node configuration tests, and
dry-runs every production Worker. Every step must succeed.

Production deployment runs from `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` after a
successful `ci` workflow on `main`. The workflow owns its required secrets,
stale-main guard, deployment command, and root, fallback, and webhook
post-deploy probes.

## Token Endpoint verification

The root overlay's `GITHUB_APP_TOKEN_BROKER` binding selects the broker Worker
and `TOKEN_PROXY_ENDPOINT` supplies its canonical App endpoint URL;
the processor overlay's `GITHUB_APP_TOKEN_BROKER_TOKEN_ENDPOINT` selects the
endpoint reached through its broker Service Binding.

Terraform retains the vanity `/token*` Route targeting `cyspbot`. Worker
publication does not provision queues, attach consumers, or change routes.

For changes affecting token delivery, verify the deployed source pin, endpoint
configuration and Service Bindings together. Check canonical and vanity OAuth
responses, least-privilege issuance and action callers, and preservation of
edge-established client identity despite spoofed forwarding headers. Local
forwarding tests and credential-free probes do not establish those properties.
Before changing transport, review any dependency on the broker hostname's
public ingress controls; HTTP Service Bindings bypass them.

Verify webhook delivery through the queue and processor to the expected GitHub
reaction when changing that flow. Use the source's
[delivery recovery procedure](https://github.com/chikachow/cyspbot/blob/main/docs/deployment.md#delivery-recovery)
for failed deliveries and exhausted jobs. Never purge jobs as part of a deployment.
Check for pending runs that could republish an incompatible version. Failed
publication or probes require operator diagnosis; they do not undo published
Workers or Terraform changes.

## Dependency tooling

Use Node 24 and the exact pnpm version in `packageManager`. Install it from the
repository root, then verify it before installing dependencies. When migrating
an existing Corepack installation, run `corepack disable pnpm` once first to
remove its pnpm shims.

```bash
npm install --global "$(node -p 'require("./package.json").packageManager')"
node --run pnpm:check
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
```

CI installs the manifest pin with `pnpm/action-setup`. The local `check` command
retains the version guard for developer environments. `pmOnFail: ignore` keeps
the lockfile as one YAML document for GitHub's dependency graph; direct pnpm commands do not automatically select or enforce the
pin. Adding config dependencies requires reviewing that compatibility assumption.

`check` validates the deployment-owned manifest and lockfile, strictly checks
peer requirements with `pnpm peers check`, and rejects avoidable lockfile
duplication. The single CI job runs these checks once and rejects lockfile changes. The full
`source:check` separately validates the pinned source tree.
Peer validation reads the lockfile; deduplication checks disable lifecycle scripts. Ordinary
resolution permits intermediate peer conflicts, while `autoInstallPeers: false`
keeps required peers explicit.

`autoDedupe` consolidates compatible resolutions during updates, including across
workspace projects outside a command's filter. Frozen installs leave the graph
unchanged; `lockfile.includeResolutionSettings` records the selected deduplication
and linking settings.
`verifyDepsBeforeRun: error` stops pnpm scripts when dependencies are stale; it
does not guard `node --run`, so install explicitly before validation.

Dependency resolution uses a three-day release age, aligned with npm Dependabot
cooldown where configured. Frozen installs also verify lockfile supply-chain
policy. Dependency build scripts require explicit `allowBuilds` decisions;
`strictDepBuilds` rejects unreviewed builds.

The source submodule keeps its own toolchain pin. `scripts/source-pnpm.mjs` reads
that pin and invokes `pnpm with <version>` from the source directory. This also
selects the version for nested pnpm commands, so deployment and source upgrades
can merge independently. Use the launcher for source commands; an outer
`pnpm -C` invocation does not select the source pin.

## Consolidated CI

The single `ci` job runs the full source checks, all deployment-local checks and
production dry-runs. Source and private dependencies retain their own pinned pnpm
versions and frozen lockfiles. Source validation runs locally on every CI run.
The final guard rejects tracked changes against `HEAD`, including staged changes,
and rejects untracked or modified source files.

Sharing one runner saves repeated setup and per-job minute rounding, at the cost
of serial feedback and a larger rerun unit. Production deployment remains in its
separate workflow with its existing exact-revision checkout, freshness checks,
production environment, credentials and live probes.

pull_request.body:
Bumps the cloudflare-workers-sdk group with 3 updates: [@cloudflare/vitest-plugin](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/tree/HEAD/packages/vitest-plugin), [@cloudflare/workers-types](https://github.com/cloudflare/workerd) and [wrangler](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/tree/HEAD/packages/wrangler). Updates `@cloudflare/vitest-plugin` from 1.4.3 to 1.4.7
Release notes

Sourced from @​cloudflare/vitest-plugin's releases.

@​cloudflare/vitest-plugin@​1.4.6

Patch Changes

  • #15708 3464abc Thanks @​samstarling! - Dispose Workflow step results and introspection modifiers after use

    Release RPC resources deterministically during local Workflow execution and introspection. This prevents undisposed RPC warnings and requests being cancelled after their execution context has ended. Live step results retain their original data shape, including typed-array offsets and backing buffers. Callbacks that finish after a step times out also release their results, cancelling unused streams without delaying retries.

    Disposing an introspector still aborts the instance if modifier acquisition failed, without introducing a teardown error. Non-stream results containing function-valued array properties are rejected according to the serialisable-output contract, instead of silently discarding those properties during storage normalisation.

  • #15846 a88cac4 Thanks @​oddharsh! - Fail with an error instead of hanging when local dev requests can't work under Bun

    Bun's fetch() ignores the undici dispatcheroven-sh/bun#39247createTestHarness()'s server.fetch() and server.getWorker()'s fetch(), email() and scheduled() now throw a UserError, requests to the dev server URL get a 503 naming the cause, and starting remote bindings throws a UserError. Each of these used to hang with no error. server.getWorker().getEnv() and getExport() keep working under Bun.

  • Updated dependencies [4508172, 61fc739, 3464abc, a88cac4, 262021d]:

    • wrangler@4.151.3
    • miniflare@5.20261019.1-beta

@​cloudflare/vitest-plugin@​1.4.5

Patch Changes

  • #16135 329d757 Thanks @​Zyles! - Fix test runs slowing down file after file, and stalling, with isolate: false

    With isolate: false, Vitest hands a worker's module runner to the pool again for every test file the worker runs, and the pool wrapped the runner's module fetches in one more layer each time, so imports got slower with every file until runs stalled. The pool now patches each module runner once.

  • Updated dependencies [37ab91c, 0ae7926]:

    • miniflare@5.20261019.0-beta
    • wrangler@4.151.2

@​cloudflare/vitest-plugin@​1.4.4

Patch Changes

  • Updated dependencies [e1d1b77, e13d5cc, 42c6912, 4a5377f]:
    • miniflare@5.20261012.1-beta
    • wrangler@4.151.1

Sourced from @​cloudflare/vitest-plugin's changelog.

1.4.7

Patch Changes

  • Updated dependencies [80a9f96, 08f22d3, 2878645, a4eb57d, 182d6de]:

1.4.6

Each of these used to hang with no error. server.getWorker().getEnv() and getExport() keep working under Bun.

1.4.5

Patch Changes

  • #16135 329d757 Thanks @​Zyles! - Fix test runs slowing down file after file, and stalling, with isolate: false

    With isolate: false, Vitest hands a worker's module runner to the pool again for every test file the worker runs, and the pool wrapped the runner's module fetches in one more layer each time, so imports got slower with every file until runs stalled. Commits
  • See full diff in compare view

Updates `wrangler` from 4.151.0 to 4.152.0
Release notes

Sourced from wrangler's releases.

wrangler@4.151.3

Patch Changes

  • #15611 4508172 Thanks @​taylorlee! - Allow wrangler dev to start module Workers without a default export

    Previously, wrangler dev failed to start module Workers that exported only named entrypoints, such as RPC services, unless an unused default export was added. These Workers now start normally in local development without that workaround.

  • #16370 61fc739 Thanks @​WalshyDev! - Fetch the remote config diff from the configured compliance region

    When a Worker was last deployed from the dashboard, wrangler deploy and wrangler versions upload download its remote configuration to compare with the local one. These requests ignored the compliance_region field in the Wrangler configuration file and only honoured the CLOUDFLARE_COMPLIANCE_REGION environment variable. A FedRAMP High Worker configured through the config file would send them to api.cloudflare.com instead of api.fed.cloudflare.com, and the deploy would fail with authentication errors. They now use the same compliance region as the rest of the deploy.

  • #15846 a88cac4 Thanks @​oddharsh! - Fail with an error instead of hanging when local dev requests can't work under Bun

    Bun's fetch() ignores the undici dispatcheroven-sh/bun#39247createTestHarness()'s server.fetch() and server.getWorker()'s fetch(), email() and scheduled() now throw a UserError, requests to the dev server URL get a 503 naming the cause, and starting remote bindings throws a UserError. Each of these used to hang with no error. server.getWorker().getEnv() and getExport() keep working under Bun.

  • #16359 262021d Thanks @​tw4! - Stop --strict deploys and version uploads from aborting when the API omits optional binding fields

    Previously, wrangler deploy --strict and wrangler versions upload --strict could report a destructive change for an unchanged configuration, for example an R2 bucket in the default jurisdiction, because a field the API left out was compared as removed. Missing and unset optional fields are now treated as equal, so these commands proceed when the local configuration matches the deployed Worker.

oxfmt v0.74.0

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • 5605362 oxfmt: Validate editorconfig as like oxfmtrc (#27778) (leaysgur)

⚡ Performance

  • e220293 formatter: Check only the operator suppression mark in is_quiet (#27952) (leaysgur)

  • a342f7e formatter: Skip comment handling for nodes with no comment near them (#27557) (leaysgur)
  • d8ce750 formatter: Write string literals with swapped quotes into the arena (#27558) (Yuji Sugiura)
  • 1c393c0 formatter_core: Skip scanning texts with nothing to rewrite (#27561) (leaysgur)
  • 1d3ef10 formatter_core: Keep the embedded IR when nothing in it is rewritten (#27673) (leaysgur)

📚 Documentation

  • 1325225 oxfmt: Update useless comment prefix (#27956) (leaysgur)
  • d0dd140 formatter: Note lossy cooked round-trip in template embeds (#27944) (leaysgur)

pull_request.body:
Bumps the vite group with 1 update: [vite](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/tree/HEAD/packages/vite). Updates `vite` from 8.3.4 to 8.3.5
Release notes

Sourced from vite's releases.

v8.3.5

Bug Fixes

  • build: handle missing chunk import maps (#23777) (8d7623d)
  • build: include preload dependencies to chunk import map hashing (#23793) (4d16e7c)
  • bundled-dev: apply server.origin to asset URLs (#23683) (52ba877)
  • bundled-dev: declare utf-8 charset in fallback page (#23846) (197daf6)
  • bundled-dev: ignore build.chunkImportMap (#23685) (cfe917d)
  • bundled-dev: include user import.meta.env.* defines in the import.meta.env object (#23713) (6019aa7)
  • bundled-dev: map forwarded error stacks through the bundle source maps (#23741) (11fe1e4)
  • bundled-dev: normalize served output files (#23684) (df4e02c)
  • bundled-dev: stop hmr propagation at modules that are no longer imported (#23839) (7471e8c)
  • css: don't fail on a literal % in url() (#23676) (50b382d)
  • deps: update all non-major dependencies (#23731) (cf80aa5)
  • deps: update all non-major dependencies (#23826) (77d8373)
  • deps: update rolldown-related dependencies (#23733) (43f0d05)
  • deps: update rolldown-related dependencies (#23827) (c2e0418)
  • optimizer: fall back to yarn.lock for lockfile hash (#23667) (f206096)
  • optimizer: scan oxc.jsxInject imports (#23758) (38f3cb4)
  • optimizer: skip patches dir check for yarn.lock fallback (#23725) (8e890e1)
  • optimizer: skip patches dir hash for nub lockfile (#23761) (a7d5696)
  • resolve: support subpath imports with multiple # (#23631) (0d86b34)
  • resolve: update resolve.exports to 2.0.4 (#23739) (4ea708a)
  • server: handle socket errors on upgrade requests not taken by the HMR server (#23728) (c2c9ef4)
  • server: only strip base when path matches a full segment (#23641) (3dfde87)

Performance Improvements

  • ssr: extract inline source maps without a regexp (#23775) (6a02780)

Miscellaneous Chores

  • migrate to Oxlint (#23746) (5b73935)

Code Refactoring

  • deps: replace @vercel/detect-agent with std-env (#23744) (ce4293f)
  • dev: consolidate moduleURL to file path utilities (#23828) (df7b40e)
  • dev: separate import resolution from URL conversion (#23791) (6116689)
  • dev: share ModuleURL and BrowserURL conversions (#23790) (446954c)
  • dev: use ModuleURLs throughout HTML transforms (#23815) (a162990)

pull_request.body:
Bumps [knip](https://github.com/webpro-nl/knip/tree/HEAD/packages/knip) from 6.41.0 to 6.42.1.
Release notes

Sourced from knip's releases.

Release 6.42.1

  • fix(semantic-release): resolve shareable configs from extends (#2159) (4c4a5ece9148cf621f3a6e091fd3550b18f6e19a) - thanks @​giaBaoJS!
  • fix(jest): load projects entries as Jest configs (#2167) (4c22593724460890e4492ba86119d0188127f2ba) - thanks @​Cayan!
  • Update npmx.dev snapshot (4b19797b77a559f7190e9119b3a156e1ac6aef9f)
  • fix(tailwind): track packages referenced from CSS url() (#2166) (949da00abf419c1eeabdab1541ce7e5c312371b9) - thanks @​agustincastaing!
  • Add .otf to foreign file extensions (fcff4db0b88d6282569743cd779aec5a5df99862)
  • Match quoted SCSS url() values within a single line (2c5c2a2efab8f08be538bfe1f40982cb6f0fca3c)
  • fix(bun): treat bun test arguments as path filters (#2165) (5f3a7fb526d3eca7561aacfc9d0ac60056525206) - thanks @​jakeleventhal!
  • fix(vitest): use default test entries when config has no test key (#2170) (7ee576ccd461f719b533e3783a5b58391ce89e91) - thanks @​fixfon!

Release 6.42.0

  • fix: add bun 1.4.3 check subcommand (#2131) (09129b8aaa554ffae2ff8f42a5ff4d6994eb7759) - thanks @​NimmLor!
  • Detect pnpm workspaces correctly around packages: (resolve #2133, close #2134) (d1cc0928be54e6cac9668460d9f6a21e3a94f818)
  • fix(github-actions): resolve working-directory nested under checkout path (#2136) (87e051e45f12c107cc25ed08bba962b95bb23b51) - thanks @​kenny-ish!
  • fix(nx): track local generator and executor entry points (#2117) (#2121) (558407f51b5fdf4460275b69950676e7bace35d5) - thanks @​DreamLongYT!
  • Update dependency bun to v1.4.3 (#2137) (71f90bf6d5fb2675430f60416e403851f9cb2cfe) - thanks @​renovate[bot]!
  • docs(react-router): note to run react-router typegen before Knip (#2140) (f21ce9a9f1e3264cad1b763cf31ec2c177fb8656) - thanks @​MannXo!
  • fix: normalize scoped binary names (close #2143) (c8509c4e45e1c343da707c26877a0a6584f6bc11)
  • Clarify plugin implementation boundaries (c5a67f59d351e8d26dc6ecbbd3c3193e313772a4)
  • fix(jest): treat mocked and required dependencies as used (#2141) (3eaf1ba16045a3ac22f0717c4f1252312298bb76) - thanks @​TkDodo!
  • fix: preserve root-only plugins for trailing-slash cwd (#2139) (7f0db0e7670bfd18fab081b522a104f787829f7d) - thanks @​sean0407!
  • fix(nx): resolve run-commands script paths from the target cwd (#2151) (516bd9a324303653978528f582287c857846fcc8) - thanks @​JeanBeaurepaire!
  • Resolve Nx run-commands loader paths from the target cwd (fa8ca13e1345115d30122900ab68db7339487502)
  • Add @​solidjs/vite-plugin plugin (#2144) (579a88d306429694be43590efb50cb72067551ba) - thanks @​everton-dgn!
  • feat: add filesystem-routing plugin (#2145) (1abd9e1875bae36b0baf77f5864aab849d1528a8) - thanks @​everton-dgn!
  • Support tags in line comments (resolve #1924) (5abef4846e20f09fd4d0ee8dc2513ce50b616cdb)
  • Keep resolveFromAST to static values in plugin guide (4cd353fd9ecb780228a63069080586a46ba6a8f2)
  • fix(solidjs-vite-plugin): keep entry overrides in production (#2155) (e4b5f890787da07824cc174cb624396f2133ff06) - thanks @​everton-dgn!
  • feat(angular): resolve styleUrl and styleUrls of @​Component (#2157) (c20d4d720c586c9c5dc6e3d1a6ea60c557688bfa) - thanks @​Cayan!
  • Update npmx.dev snapshot (59eb873f3beecf40b7aed9579bd29e1ab8b631f0)
  • fix(next): recognize Turbopack alias targets (#2156) (1d44f6a1a39c5557c1e215c7cf9db17937967344) - thanks @​jakeleventhal!
  • fix: preserve re-exports from framework entries (#2154) (263ce20408a77b2473c555f304ad3b55c696b6a6) - thanks @​jakeleventhal!
  • feat(solidjs-vite-plugin): follow Solid's SSR and client mode entry rules (#2148) (d711231eae14d8ecac562d73078125f3b30dc8fd) - thanks @​everton-dgn!
  • feat(filesystem-routing): read route options from Vite configs (#2149) (585f206ca52d54e30f2068c818e1b33b50085459) - thanks @​everton-dgn!
  • feat(filesystem-routing): resolve routes from the Vite root (#2150) (8cc0cb0c9ff09463cad30817c8cf78cbc48b7ed6) - thanks @​everton-dgn!
  • fix: track namespace members in Promise.all imports (#2162) (3f17cdfce7a0f90e2599a7074291c4c875fe8244) - thanks @​everton-dgn!
  • Update a few dependencies (161dbed3ccffa574e3a9493ddb20842eefa26af8)
  • Fix Solid setup fixture coverage (ebe4180785667f6ff85c1e6ce2a11226713b2d5a)
  • Migrate shell script parsing to unbash v6 (f86044c6760ac4f27e564f15feeae907cba3d297)
  • Add sponsors: @​pennylane-hq, @​agentscore, @​oblique-security (thank you!) (57ff23eb430aaece73e02574923cabc6016a920b)
  • Stop pairing Promise.all imports and bindings after a spread (5bd2c64eaf92f82a316d8fa6551acdb1d6c48c32)
  • Update some stats (dd02ddeb235dd516cf93db99dda2180b0eb09a97)
  • fix(nx): read karmaConfig from target options (#2164) (4e1e4bc18f6d2f2705d729c375a20bd1679b8c0f) - thanks @​Cayan!
  • Add tsrs plugin (#2163) (ba09126c023a2c408de8d7dae3bf6ab97e420966) - thanks @​jakeleventhal!
  • Drop redundant containingFilePath from plugin config inputs (ffb6caf02891d29eee41c7a0ecf147312dbe7205)
  • Resolve Nx target option configs from the workspace root (52c5233aa905124c5b30c0bb7f9b0b25cd4260c6)
Commits
  • ee32ee6 Release knip@6.42.1
  • 7ee576c fix(vitest): use default test entries when config has no test key (#2170)
  • 5f3a7fb fix(bun): treat bun test arguments as path filters (#2165)
  • 2c5c2a2 Match quoted SCSS url() values within a single line
  • fcff4db Add .otf to foreign file extensions
  • 949da00 fix(tailwind): track packages referenced from CSS url() (#2166)
  • 4c22593 fix(jest): load projects entries as Jest configs (#2167)
  • 4c4a5ec fix(semantic-release): resolve shareable configs from extends (#2159)
  • 8aa7d0e Release knip@6.42.0
  • 52c5233 Resolve Nx target option configs from the workspace root
  • Additional commits viewable in compare view

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Action completed."}],"structuredContent":{"pull_request":{"url":"https://github.com/chikachow/cyspbot-deploy/pull/110","number":110,"state":"open","merged":false,"mergeable":true,"draft":false,"body":"Bumps the oxc-tooling group with 2 updates: [oxfmt](https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/tree/HEAD/npm/oxfmt) and [oxlint](https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/tree/HEAD/npm/oxlint). Updates `oxfmt` from 0.73.0 to 0.74.0
Release notes

Sourced from oxfmt's releases.

oxfmt v0.74.0

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • e236de0 formatter_tests: Skip conformance spec calls with non-literal options (#27957) (leaysgur)
  • 782ab6e linter: Search string values without UTF-8 conversion (#26716) (Dunqing)
  • a5d8184 jsdoc: Parse code spans after quotes in descriptions (#27955) (leaysgur)
  • 2645d2c formatter_markdown: Treat link destinations and footnote references as opaque to code span fences (#27948) (leaysgur)
  • 4d8195c formatter_yaml: Keep a root plain scalar starting with a document marker verbatim (#27947) (leaysgur)
  • 529b057 formatter_core: Keep front matter verbatim when body starts with indented delimiter (#27946) (leaysgur)
  • c22a9b2 formatter: Treat static block with only empty statements as empty (#27945) (leaysgur)
  • d3ff3f6 formatter/jsdoc: Write descriptions as written to not close the comment (#27823) (leaysgur)
  • c4c1727 formatter/sort_imports: Keep comments after the last import (#27822) (leaysgur)
  • a64677e formatter: Print JSDoc embedded snippets with LF (#27821) (leaysgur)
  • 2c1cc20 formatter: Keep comment only Vue bindings as-is (#27820) (leaysgur)
  • 1bf236d formatter/sort_imports: Do not use comments as import source (#27819) (leaysgur)
  • 52ee29d formatter_yaml: Never start col-0 line with document marker or BOM (#27818) (leaysgur)
  • 81c75e7 formatter/css: Keep glued css-in-js statement placeholders glued (#27814) (leaysgur)
  • a1ef7f4 formatter: Keep typecast parens in same-operator binary and arrow chain (#27812) (leaysgur)
  • de110ce formatter: Keep more parens around TSInstantiationExpression (#27811) (leaysgur)
  • 8b02e90 formatter_json: Reject invalid JSON instead of dropping them (#27785) (leaysgur)
  • 6fe4c1b formatter: Treat lone CR in JSX text and argument blank lines (#27780) (leaysgur)
  • 5605362 oxfmt: Validate editorconfig as like oxfmtrc (#27778) (leaysgur)
  • 5b2acb0 formatter_core: Report error position releative to CRLF source (#27777) (leaysgur)
  • c78e80e formatter_core: Report parse error positions relative to the BOM-headed source (#27776) (leaysgur)

pull_request.body:
Bumps [knip](https://github.com/webpro-nl/knip/tree/HEAD/packages/knip) from 6.41.0 to 6.42.1.
Release notes

Sourced from knip's releases.

Release 6.42.1

  • fix(semantic-release): resolve shareable configs from extends (#2159) (4c4a5ece9148cf621f3a6e091fd3550b18f6e19a) - thanks @​giaBaoJS!
  • fix(jest): load projects entries as Jest configs (#2167) (4c22593724460890e4492ba86119d0188127f2ba) - thanks @​Cayan!
  • Update npmx.dev snapshot (4b19797b77a559f7190e9119b3a156e1ac6aef9f)
  • fix(tailwind): track packages referenced from CSS url() (#2166) (949da00abf419c1eeabdab1541ce7e5c312371b9) - thanks @​agustincastaing!
  • Add .otf to foreign file extensions (fcff4db0b88d6282569743cd779aec5a5df99862)
  • Match quoted SCSS url() values within a single line (2c5c2a2efab8f08be538bfe1f40982cb6f0fca3c)
  • fix(bun): treat bun test arguments as path filters (#2165) (5f3a7fb526d3eca7561aacfc9d0ac60056525206) - thanks @​jakeleventhal!
  • fix(vitest): use default test entries when config has no test key (#2170) (7ee576ccd461f719b533e3783a5b58391ce89e91) - thanks @​fixfon!

Release 6.42.0

  • fix: add bun 1.4.3 check subcommand (#2131) (09129b8aaa554ffae2ff8f42a5ff4d6994eb7759) - thanks @​NimmLor!
  • Detect pnpm workspaces correctly around packages: (resolve #2133, close #2134) (d1cc0928be54e6cac9668460d9f6a21e3a94f818)
  • fix(github-actions): resolve working-directory nested under checkout path (#2136) (87e051e45f12c107cc25ed08bba962b95bb23b51) - thanks @​kenny-ish!
  • fix(nx): track local generator and executor entry points (#2117) (#2121) (558407f51b5fdf4460275b69950676e7bace35d5) - thanks @​DreamLongYT!
  • Update dependency bun to v1.4.3 (#2137) (71f90bf6d5fb2675430f60416e403851f9cb2cfe) - thanks @​renovate[bot]!
  • docs(react-router): note to run react-router typegen before Knip (#2140) (f21ce9a9f1e3264cad1b763cf31ec2c177fb8656) - thanks @​MannXo!
  • fix: normalize scoped binary names (close #2143) (c8509c4e45e1c343da707c26877a0a6584f6bc11)
  • Clarify plugin implementation boundaries (c5a67f59d351e8d26dc6ecbbd3c3193e313772a4)
  • fix(jest): treat mocked and required dependencies as used (#2141) (3eaf1ba16045a3ac22f0717c4f1252312298bb76) - thanks @​TkDodo!
  • fix: preserve root-only plugins for trailing-slash cwd (#2139) (7f0db0e7670bfd18fab081b522a104f787829f7d) - thanks @​sean0407!
  • fix(nx): resolve run-commands script paths from the target cwd (#2151) (516bd9a324303653978528f582287c857846fcc8) - thanks @​JeanBeaurepaire!
  • Resolve Nx run-commands loader paths from the target cwd (fa8ca13e1345115d30122900ab68db7339487502)
  • Add @​solidjs/vite-plugin plugin (#2144) (579a88d306429694be43590efb50cb72067551ba) - thanks @​everton-dgn!
  • feat: add filesystem-routing plugin (#2145) (1abd9e1875bae36b0baf77f5864aab849d1528a8) - thanks @​everton-dgn!
  • Support tags in line comments (resolve #1924) (5abef4846e20f09fd4d0ee8dc2513ce50b616cdb)
  • Keep resolveFromAST to static values in plugin guide (4cd353fd9ecb780228a63069080586a46ba6a8f2)
  • fix(solidjs-vite-plugin): keep entry overrides in production (#2155) (e4b5f890787da07824cc174cb624396f2133ff06) - thanks @​everton-dgn!
  • feat(angular): resolve styleUrl and styleUrls of @​Component (#2157) (c20d4d720c586c9c5dc6e3d1a6ea60c557688bfa) - thanks @​Cayan!
  • Update npmx.dev snapshot (59eb873f3beecf40b7aed9579bd29e1ab8b631f0)
  • fix(next): recognize Turbopack alias targets (#2156) (1d44f6a1a39c5557c1e215c7cf9db17937967344) - thanks @​jakeleventhal!
  • fix: preserve re-exports from framework entries (#2154) (263ce20408a77b2473c555f304ad3b55c696b6a6) - thanks @​jakeleventhal!
  • feat(solidjs-vite-plugin): follow Solid's SSR and client mode entry rules (#2148) (d711231eae14d8ecac562d73078125f3b30dc8fd) - thanks @​everton-dgn!
  • feat(filesystem-routing): read route options from Vite configs (#2149) (585f206ca52d54e30f2068c818e1b33b50085459) - thanks @​everton-dgn!
  • feat(filesystem-routing): resolve routes from the Vite root (#2150) (8cc0cb0c9ff09463cad30817c8cf78cbc48b7ed6) - thanks @​everton-dgn!
  • fix: track namespace members in Promise.all imports (#2162) (3f17cdfce7a0f90e2599a7074291c4c875fe8244) - thanks @​everton-dgn!
  • Update a few dependencies (161dbed3ccffa574e3a9493ddb20842eefa26af8)
  • Fix Solid setup fixture coverage (ebe4180785667f6ff85c1e6ce2a11226713b2d5a)
  • Migrate shell script parsing to unbash v6 (f86044c6760ac4f27e564f15feeae907cba3d297)
  • Add sponsors: @​pennylane-hq, @​agentscore, @​oblique-security (thank you!) (57ff23eb430aaece73e02574923cabc6016a920b)
  • Stop pairing Promise.all imports and bindings after a spread (5bd2c64eaf92f82a316d8fa6551acdb1d6c48c32)
  • Update some stats (dd02ddeb235dd516cf93db99dda2180b0eb09a97)
  • fix(nx): read karmaConfig from target options (#2164) (4e1e4bc18f6d2f2705d729c375a20bd1679b8c0f) - thanks @​Cayan!
  • Add tsrs plugin (#2163) (ba09126c023a2c408de8d7dae3bf6ab97e420966) - thanks @​jakeleventhal!
  • Drop redundant containingFilePath from plugin config inputs (ffb6caf02891d29eee41c7a0ecf147312dbe7205)
  • Resolve Nx target option configs from the workspace root (52c5233aa905124c5b30c0bb7f9b0b25cd4260c6)

Patch Changes

  • #15708 3464abc Thanks @​samstarling! - Dispose Workflow step results and introspection modifiers after use

    Release RPC resources deterministically during local Workflow execution and introspection. This prevents undisposed RPC warnings and requests being cancelled after their execution context has ended. Live step results retain their original data shape, including typed-array offsets and backing buffers. Callbacks that finish after a step times out also release their results, cancelling unused streams without delaying retries.

    Disposing an introspector still aborts the instance if modifier acquisition failed, without introducing a teardown error. Non-stream results containing function-valued array properties are rejected according to the serialisable-output contract, instead of silently discarding those properties during storage normalisation.

  • #15846 a88cac4 Thanks @​oddharsh! - Fail with an error instead of hanging when local dev requests can't work under Bun

    Bun's fetch() ignores the undici dispatcheroven-sh/bun#39247createTestHarness()'s server.fetch() and server.getWorker()'s fetch(), email() and scheduled() now throw a UserError, requests to the dev server URL get a 503 naming the cause, and starting remote bindings throws a UserError. Each of these used to hang with no error. server.getWorker().getEnv() and getExport() keep working under Bun.

L130: # undici vulnerable to Denial of Service via unhandled error on excessive content-encodings
L131: 
L132: High
L133: 
L134: 【70†mcollina】 published GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c Oct 15, 2026
L135: 
L136: ## Package
L137: 
L138: undici (【71†npm】)

L140: ## Affected versions
L141:

L155: ## Description
L156: ### Impact
L157: undici's `fetch()` crashes the Node.js process when a malicious server returns a response with more than five content codings and closes the connection before sending the body. undici rejects such responses (a content-encoding limit), but it created the internal response stream before that check and returned without attaching an error listener or aborting the request.
L158: The early close then surfaces a content-length mismatch on that orphaned internal stream, which Node.js treats as an unhandled `error` and terminates the process. A remote, unauthenticated server can trigger this with a single response, even when the application correctly catches the `fetch()` rejection. undici 6.x, 7.x, and 8.x are affected.
L159: ### Patches
L160: 
L161: Upgrade to `6.29.1`, `7.30.1`, or `8.12.2`. undici now validates the content-encoding chain before creating the internal body stream and aborts the response when the limit is exceeded, so no error can surface on an orphaned stream.

L165: None.

L23: ## packages【6†#】
L24: 
L25: Besides settings, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` defines the root of the 【7†workspace】 and enables you to include / exclude directories from the workspace. If the `packages` field is omitted, only the root package is included in the workspace.
L26: 
L27: For example:
L28: pnpm-workspace.yaml
L29: 
L30:     `packages:
L31:       # specify a package in a direct subdir of the root
L32:       - 'my-app'
L33:       # all packages in direct subdirs of packages/
L34:       - 'packages/*'
L35:       # all packages in subdirs of components/
L36:       - 'components/**'
L37:       # exclude packages that are inside test directories
L38:       - '!**/test/**'
L39:     `
L40: 
L41: The root package is always included, even when custom location wildcards are used.
L42: A pattern may be written with a `./` prefix, may contain `.` and `..` segments, and may repeat slashes: `./packages/*` and `packages//*` select the same projects, and `!./packages/legacy` excludes the same directory that `!packages/legacy` does. A `*` never matches a name beginning with a dot, so `packages/*` skips `packages/.cache`; name such a directory explicitly to include it.
L43: 
L44: Note
L45: pnpm reads the workspace from `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, not from the `workspaces` field of the root `package.json`. Since v12.4.1, a root manifest that declares a non-empty `workspaces` array in a project with no `pnpm-workspace.yaml` gets a warning, because such an install silently links no project at all.
L46: 
L47: Catalogs are also defined in the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` file. See 【8†Catalogs】 for details.
L48: pnpm-workspace.yaml
L49: 
L50:     `packages:
L51:       - 'packages/*'
L52: 
L53:     catalog:
L54:       chalk: ^4.1.2
L55: 
L56:     catalogs:
L57:       react16:
L58:         react: ^16.7.0
L59:         react-dom: ^16.7.0
L60:       react17:
L61:         react: ^17.10.0
L62:         react-dom: ^17.10.0
L63:     `
L64: ## packageConfigs【9†#】
L65: 
L66: Added in: v11.0.0
L67: 
L68: Allows setting project-specific configuration for individual workspace packages. This replaces workspace project-specific `.npmrc` files.
L69: 
L70: `packageConfigs` can be specified as a map of package names to config objects:
L71: 
L72: pnpm-workspace.yaml
L73: 
L74:     `packages:
L75:       - "packages/project-1"
L76:       - "packages/project-2"
L77:     packageConfigs:
L78:       "project-1":
L79:         saveExact: true
L80:       "project-2":
L81:         savePrefix: "~"
L82:     `
L83: Or as an array of pattern-matched rules:
L84: 
L85: pnpm-workspace.yaml
L86: 
L87:     `packages:
L88:       - "packages/project-1"
L89:       - "packages/project-2"
L90:     packageConfigs:
L91:       - match: ["project-1", "project-2"]
L92:         modulesDir: "node_modules"
L93:         saveExact: true
L94:     `
L95: Settings that shape resolution or the layout of `node_modules` (`overrides`, `hoist`, `modulesDir`, `saveExact`, `savePrefix`, and their neighbours) take effect per project only where each project has its own lockfile, that is with 【10†`sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`】. A workspace on the default shared lockfile has one resolution for every project, so pnpm reports which entries it ignored instead of applying them silently.

L0: # Dependency Resolution Settings
L1: ### overrides【0†#】
L2: 
L3: This field allows you to instruct pnpm to override any dependency in the dependency graph, including peer dependencies. This is useful for enforcing all your packages to use a single version of a dependency, backporting a fix, replacing a dependency with a fork, or removing an unused dependency.
L4: 
L5: Note that the overrides field can only be set at the root of the project.
L6: 
L7: An example of the `overrides` field:
L8: pnpm-workspace.yaml
L9: 
L10:     `overrides:
L11:       "foo": "^1.0.0"
L12:       "quux": "npm:@myorg/quux@^1.0.0"
L13:       "bar@^2.1.0": "3.0.0"
L14:       "qar@1>zoo": "2"
L15:     `
L16: 
L17: You may specify the package the overridden dependency belongs to by separating the package selector from the dependency selector with a ">", for example `qar@1>zoo` will only override the `zoo` dependency of `qar@1`, not for any other dependencies.
L18: To keep an overridden version in sync with the version used elsewhere in your workspace, define the version in a 【1†catalog】 and reference it with the `catalog:` protocol. This way the version is maintained in a single place and referenced from both your dependencies and your overrides:
L19: 
L20: pnpm-workspace.yaml
L21: 
L22:     `catalog:
L23:       foo: "^1.0.0"
L24: 
L25:     overrides:
L26:       foo: "catalog:"
L27:     `
L28: 
L29: You may also reference a named catalog with `catalog:<name>`. See 【1†Catalogs】 for more details.
L30: If you find that your use of a certain package doesn't require one of its dependencies, you may use `-` to remove it. For example, if package `foo@1.0.0` requires a large package named `bar` for a function that you don't use, removing it could reduce install time:
L31: 
L32: pnpm-workspace.yaml
L33: 
L34:     `overrides:
L35:       "foo@1.0.0>bar": "-"
L36:     `
L37: 
L38: This feature is especially useful with `optionalDependencies`, where most optional packages can be safely skipped.
L39: #### Convergence overrides【2†#】
L40: 
L41: Added in: v11.13.0
L42: 
L43: A selector with an empty range — `"pkg@"` — is a convergence override. Unlike a regular override, which rewrites every matching edge unconditionally, a convergence override rewrites a dependency edge only when its version satisfies the range that edge declares:
L44: 
L45: pnpm-workspace.yaml
L46: 
L47:     `overrides:
L48:       "form-data@": 4.0.6
L49:     `
L50: With the above, a dependency that declares `form-data: "^4.0.5"` is pinned to `4.0.6`, while one that declares `^3.0.0` keeps its own resolution. This lets compatible consumers converge on a single version — now and for any dependent added in the future — without forcing an incompatible version on the rest of the graph.
L51: 
L52: Rules:
L53:   * The value must be an exact version. A range, a dist-tag, or a `-` removal fails with `ERR_PNPM_INVALID_CONVERGENCE_OVERRIDE`. A `catalog:` reference is allowed as long as the catalog entry resolves to an exact version.
L54:   * Only plain semver edges participate. Edges declared with `workspace:`, `catalog:`, `npm:`, a dist-tag, or a git/URL specifier have no meaningful "satisfies" relation and are left untouched.
L55:   * Convergence overrides cannot be combined with a parent selector: `"parent>pkg@"` is rejected.
L56:   * A regular override always wins over a convergence override for the same edge.
L57: When a full resolution finds that every declared range also admits a newer version, pnpm warns that the override is stale and names the version to converge on instead.
L58: 
L59: Note
L60: 
L61: Before v11.13.0, an empty range in an override selector was undocumented and behaved like a bare (unscoped) override.
L62: #### Overriding peer dependencies【3†#】
L63: 
L64: Overrides also apply to `peerDependencies`. The behavior depends on the type of version specifier used in the override:
L65:   * Semver ranges (e.g., `^1.0.0`), workspace, and catalog protocols: the peer dependency is overridden and remains a peer dependency.
L66:   * Non-range specifiers such as `link:` or `file:` protocols: the peer dependency is overridden and moved to `dependencies`, since these are not valid peer dependency ranges.
L67:   * Removal (`-`): the peer dependency is removed entirely.
L68: 
L69: For example, to override the `react` peer dependency of `react-dom`:
L70: pnpm-workspace.yaml
L71: 
L72:     `overrides:
L73:       "react-dom>react": "18.1.0"
L74:     `
L75: ### packageExtensions【4†#】
L76: 
L77: The `packageExtensions` fields offer a way to extend the existing package definitions with additional information. For example, if `react-redux` should have `react-dom` in its `peerDependencies` but it has not, it is possible to patch `react-redux` using `packageExtensions`:
L78: 
L79: pnpm-workspace.yaml
L80: 
L81:     `packageExtensions:
L82:       react-redux:
L83:         peerDependencies:
L84:           react-dom: "*"
L85:     `
L86: The keys in `packageExtensions` are package names or package names and semver ranges, so it is possible to patch only some versions of a package:
L87: 
L88: pnpm-workspace.yaml
L89: 
L90:     `packageExtensions:
L91:       react-redux@1:
L92:         peerDependencies:
L93:           react-dom: "*"
L94:     `
L95: 
L96: The following fields may be extended using `packageExtensions`: `dependencies`, `optionalDependencies`, `peerDependencies`, and `peerDependenciesMeta`.
L97: 
L98: A bigger example:
L99: pnpm-workspace.yaml
L100: 
L101:     `packageExtensions:
L102:       express@1:
L103:         optionalDependencies:
L104:           typescript: "2"
L105:       fork-ts-checker-webpack-plugin:
L106:         dependencies:
L107:           "@babel/core": "1"
L108:         peerDependencies:
L109:           eslint: ">= 6"
L110:         peerDependenciesMeta:
L111:           eslint:
L112:             optional: true
L113:     `
L114: 
L115: Tip
L116: Together with Yarn, we maintain a database of `packageExtensions` to patch broken packages in the ecosystem. If you use `packageExtensions`, consider sending a PR upstream and contributing your extension to the 【5†`@yarnpkg/extensions`†github.com】 database.
L117: ### allowedDeprecatedVersions【6†#】
L118: 
L119: This setting allows muting deprecation warnings of specific packages.
L120: 
L121: Example:
L122: 
L123: pnpm-workspace.yaml
L124: 
L125:     `allowedDeprecatedVersions:
L126:       express: "1"
L127:       request: "*"
L128:     `
L129: 
L130: With the above configuration pnpm will not print deprecation warnings about any version of `request` and about v1 of `express`.
L131: 
L132: ### update【7†#】
L133: 
L134: Added in: v11.16.0
L135: 
L136: Settings in this section tune the 【8†`pnpm update`】 and 【9†`pnpm outdated`】 commands.
L137: #### update.ignoreDeps【10†#】
L138: 
L139: Sometimes you can't update a dependency. For instance, the latest version of the dependency started to use ESM but your project is not yet in ESM. Annoyingly, such a package will always be printed out by the `pnpm outdated` command and updated, when running `pnpm update --latest`. However, you may list packages that you don't want to upgrade in the `ignoreDeps` field:
L140: 
L141: pnpm-workspace.yaml
L142: 
L143:     `update:
L144:       ignoreDeps:
L145:       - load-json-file
L146:     `
L147: Patterns are also supported, so you may ignore any packages from a scope: `@babel/*`.
L148: #### update.changeset【11†#】

For tasks that may span context windows, use `notes` to maintain a concise checkpoint of the goal, decisions, progress, learnings and next steps. Include the window ID and item ID for every relevant user request you are currently solving as well as important actions/tool calls. You can use `history` tool to look up details with the references later. Note that every non-assistant item, such as user, developer, tool response, has an item id `[id: ...]` that is immediately after its item content. Relative note paths belong to the current thread; absolute paths may read other threads' notes, but writes are limited to the current thread.

It is a good idea to take incremental notes while you work so that you do not miss any important info. You can also use `get_context_remaining` tool to find the remaining token budget for better planning. Once the token budget is exhausted, you will lose access to the current window and continue in a fresh context window and you can only recover through `notes` and `history` tools. So be careful not to over-run the context window without any documentation.

If Previous context window id is present in `<context_window>`, it means a context reset occurred and this is a new window. After a reset, read the checkpoint and use the read-only `history` tool to recover any missing details. When a window ID and item ID are known, prefer `read_item` directly; when they are missing or uncertain, use `list_items`, or `search_contents` to locate the item first.

Treat notes and history as internal bookkeeping. Do not mention them in user-facing messages.

# Contributing

Keep changes cohesive, explicit, and grounded in the service contract.
[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) owns repository agent guidance; this document owns
validation scope and contribution requirements. Personal agent configuration
is not a prerequisite. Tool versions and command definitions remain
authoritative in `package.json`, `.nvmrc`, and the lockfile. For dependency
setup and updates, follow [dependency tooling](#dependency-tooling).

## Validation scope

Use focused checks during implementation. Before declaring a change fully
verified or ready, or opening or updating a pull request, apply the matching gate:

- **Agent instructions or prose only:** review consistency, local links, and the
  final diff; run `pnpm exec oxfmt --check <changed-markdown-files>` with the
  pinned formatter and `git diff --check`. For instruction changes, walk through
  representative triggering, safe, and unrelated tasks. Label these as static
  walkthroughs unless actual agent trials were observed. Static walkthroughs
  suffice for straightforward instruction corrections. Use observed agent trials
  to resolve material disagreements about agent behavior and before claiming
  that wording improves behavior; limit claims to what the trials establish.
  A full install and application suite are not required solely for prose changes.
- **Code, configuration, dependencies, generated artifacts, or executable
  examples:** establish dependencies with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and
  use Node 24 and the pinned pnpm to run the full `pnpm run check` and
